name: Cassiopeia
description: The Queen of Ethiopia is one of the most recognisable northern constellations, tracing a distinctive W or M shape that never sets for observers above 20° north. It lies in the heart of the Milky Way opposite the Great Bear, and is notable for containing the direction toward which our Solar System appears from the nearest stars.
funFact: From Alpha Centauri, our nearest stellar neighbour, the Sun appears as a magnitude 0.5 star near the border of Cassiopeia and Perseus — almost exactly opposite Alpha Centauri's own position in Centaurus. Any alien astronomers in the Alpha Centauri system looking for our Sun would find it in this patch of sky.
